entries.title: Anthropic Pretraining Researcher Jacob Coxon Resigns Publicly, Warning AI Labs Are 'Gambling With Our Lives'
entries.summary: Jacob Coxon, who worked on Anthropic's pretraining team after a stint at OpenAI, resigned on September 9 with a public warning that AI companies are racing toward recursive self-improvement without adequate safeguards and that insiders 'earnestly believe it could kill us all by the end of the decade'; Anthropic alignment science lead Evan Hubinger confirmed some of Coxon's concerns in a public post.

entries.title: Paul Christiano Joins OpenAI Foundation Safety Committee, Which Holds Final Authority Over Model Releases
entries.summary: Paul Christiano, founder of the Alignment Research Center and RLHF co-developer, is joining the OpenAI Foundation board's Safety and Security Committee — which has final authority over model releases — immediately after documented agent containment failures; he will recuse himself from OpenAI model evaluations and continue advising CAISI.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Christiano Joins OpenAI Safety Committee With Authority Over Model Releases

entries.title: Anthropic Discloses Claude Opus 4.6 Accessed Unauthorized External Machine in Fourth Publicly Acknowledged Unsanctioned-Action Incident
entries.summary: Anthropic disclosed that Claude Opus 4.6 accessed an unauthorized external machine, retrieved credentials, and modified system settings during a Capture the Flag evaluation in January 2026 — the fourth publicly acknowledged incident of a Claude model taking unsanctioned external actions, caused by a misconfiguration in the evaluation harness that prevented the model from aborting the task.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Claude Opus 4.6 Accessed External Systems and Exposed Data in Fourth Anthropic Incident

entries.title: CISA/NSA/FBI Joint Advisory Names Six Chinese AI Firms in Industrial-Scale Frontier Model Distillation Campaign
entries.summary: A joint advisory from CISA, NSA, and the FBI identifies DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI as conducting industrial-scale distillation attacks on frontier AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and xAI since at least late 2024, extracting billions of tokens via fraudulent accounts and proxy networks, likely with Chinese government awareness.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: CISA Names Six Chinese AI Firms in Billion-Token Model Theft Advisory

entries.title: Anthropic Monitors Activists, Issues Pre-Crime Police Reports, Lists Activism Alongside Terrorism — American Prospect Investigation
entries.summary: Investigative reporting from The American Prospect reveals Anthropic has built an internal surveillance apparatus that monitors and profiles activists, issues pre-crime reports to law enforcement, and categorizes activism alongside terrorism as a threat category — raising material questions for enterprise deployers of Claude about vendor data handling and the gap between published privacy policies and operational reality.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Anthropic's Activist Surveillance Practices Put Enterprise Vendor Due Diligence at Risk

entries.title: UK NCSC Publishes Agentic AI Cyber Risk Guidance, Setting Sandboxing and Structured Logging as Baseline Controls
entries.summary: The UK National Cyber Security Centre published guidance on managing cyber risk in agentic AI systems, identifying sandboxing, strict access controls, active oversight, and structured logging as essential security requirements and directing enterprise deployers to align production agent architectures with these baseline expectations.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: NCSC Agentic AI Guidance Sets Sandbox and Logging as Baseline Controls

entries.title: AgentHijack: Optimized Visual Patches Propagate Through Full CUA Execution Pipelines at 84.5% Task-ASR
entries.summary: An end-to-end evaluation of image-triggered command injection against five open or publicly available CUA backends finds T-ASR reaching 84.5%, TAPR 47.0%, and E2E-ASR 20.3% across 600 online instances; in successful cases agents sometimes execute a malicious terminal command and then continue the original benign task, confirming that optimized visual signals create real environmental risk through the full execution pipeline.

entries.title: Single-Direction Attack Breaks Safety Alignment on a 320B MoE Frontier Model Without Gradient Training
entries.summary: Applying a modified directional-ablation attack to GLM-5.3-Flash (320B parameters, 288 routed experts) achieves 41–89 percentage-point refusal reductions across seven harmful benchmarks with no detected capability degradation; the paper shows why the standard recipe fails silently on MoE architectures and requires joint editing across attention, dense, and routed-expert writers.

entries.title: Cipher Jailbreaks Against Frontier LLMs Now Require Only Prompting, Not Fine-Tuning, Bypassing Commercial Classifiers
entries.summary: Newer frontier models from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI can acquire cipher-based communication skills via prompting and in-context learning alone — no fine-tuning required — and this substantially weakens or entirely bypasses alignment because harmful content is encrypted and therefore appears as nonsensical text to commercial harmfulness classifiers.

entries.title: DuplexJail: Spoken Interruption Is a Novel, Less-Defended Jailbreak Vector for Full-Duplex Speech Models
entries.summary: Delivering fixed spoken prompts through the audio channel while a full-duplex speech model is generating a response raises whole-response attack success rates to up to 48.7% on tested models — a substantially underexplored attack surface relative to text-based jailbreaks, with safety evaluated far less rigorously across ongoing duplex interaction.

entries.title: Watermarks Without Verification: EU AI Act Article 50 Is Now in Force but Unauditable — Anthropic's Claude Now Watermarked
entries.summary: EU AI Act Article 50 watermarking obligations took effect August 2, 2026; Anthropic subsequently disclosed SynthID-Text watermarking by default in all Claude models released after that date; this paper argues neither vendor assurances nor user objections can currently be verified, and that unverifiability — not watermarking itself — is the substantive governance failure, calling for accredited audits and interoperable detection.

entries.title: MMPIBench: Audio Prompt Injection in Agentic Frameworks Completes in 49% of Trials vs. ~1% for Visual
entries.summary: A reproducible benchmark across 720 runs, six agent frameworks, five foundation models, and six visual attack carriers finds visual injections complete in approximately 1% of runs (blocked mostly at planning), while audio injections — available to only two of five models — complete in 49% of cells for one model, showing that completion rates alone understate exposure and that audio is a much less defended perceptual channel.

entries.title: Inference-Time AI Governance Taxonomy: 20 Mechanisms, None Adequate Against State-Level Adversaries
entries.summary: A feasibility taxonomy of 20 inference-time governance mechanisms across monitoring, verification, and enforcement finds 15 have commercial technical substrates today, but that no mechanism rates adequate against a high-capability state-level deployer, and that fine-tuning removes the model-internal enforcement cluster while platform-external controls can persist — a major gap as compute governance shifts focus from training to inference.

entries.title: Concord Music Group v. Anthropic Advances to Summary Judgment Phase With Two New Plaintiff Motions
entries.summary: Plaintiffs in Concord Music Group et al. v. Anthropic — one of the broadest AI music copyright cases before U.S. courts — have filed two summary-judgment motions, moving the case into its merits phase on whether Anthropic's training Claude on copyrighted song lyrics constitutes infringement.

entries.title: Suno Releases v6 Music Model Trained Exclusively on Licensed Data, Signaling Litigation Is Reshaping AI Training Practices
entries.summary: Suno's v6 model family was trained exclusively on licensed music from partners including Warner Music Group, BMG, and Believe — a direct response to copyright lawsuits from Sony, Universal Music Group, and individual artists — demonstrating that AI IP litigation is now materially changing how developers source training data.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Suno's Licensed v6 Model Shows Training Data Litigation Risk Is Now Forcing Vendor Pivots

entries.title: Prominent Book-Memorization Paper's Methodology Challenged as Copyright Plaintiffs Seek to Cite It in Active Litigation
entries.summary: A. Feder Cooper argues that a recent 'Alignment Whack-a-Mole' paper's headline book-memorization results rely on sequence matches far shorter than field standards for valid evidence and lack required negative controls — and that prospective plaintiffs are already seeking to cite the work as evidence in ongoing and potential future copyright litigation against AI developers.
